subject: Net terms, invoice frequency & SKU-bucket billing constraints for PO acceptance
messages:

Subject: PO prerequisites and billing cadence questions for Redwood engagement

Hi Priya,

We're getting close to signing, but Procurement has a few non-standard asks before they can issue a formal PO. Attached is our standard PO requirements spreadsheet — can you confirm whether Redwood can comply with the following items?

1) Invoice cadence: We prefer a weekly consolidated invoice per BU (one invoice for all Redwood usage for the week). Is that supported?

2) Net terms: our AP team operates on net45. Is Redwood able to accept net45 for enterprise customers?

3) PO line detail: Each invoice needs to include SKU-level line items, quantity, unit price, and our GL code (we'll populate the GL code per invoice). Can Redwood map SKU/GLO mapping to the invoice lines?

4) Discount stacking / packaging: Our procurement folks want to confirm whether discounts can be applied across SKU buckets (e.g., usage and dedicated capacity combined to reach a discount slab).

5) Minimum invoice amount + split payments: We may want smaller weekly invoices that can be below your current minimums — any constraints?

If it's easier, we can set a quick 20-minute call today to walk Procurement through the constraints and finish the PO template. Appreciate a short confirmation so our Sourcing team can proceed.

Thanks,
Marcus Lane
Senior Procurement Manager
Greenspire Health

Hi Marcus — thanks for the clear list and the PO spreadsheet. We can accommodate most of these items, but I want to validate a couple of specifics with Finance and Pricing before locking anything in. Quick answers below and proposed next steps: 

1) Invoice cadence: We can produce a weekly consolidated invoice per BU. We typically default to monthly consolidated invoicing, but weekly is supported for enterprise customers if a minimum invoice amount is met.

2) Net terms: Redwood standard is net30. We can support net45 for enterprise accounts subject to Finance sign-off and underwriting — I will escalate.

3) PO line detail: We can emit SKU-level lines and include a PO ID and GL code in the invoice reference fields. We will need the mapping table (SKU -> Greenspire GL code) and an ERP sample to validate CSV ingestion.

4) Discount stacking / packaging: In general we allow aggregation across usage and Reserved/Dedicated SKUs to qualify for tiered discounts, but commit-level thresholds are applied across the combined spend and may require a contractual commitment (term length or minimum spend).

5) Minimum invoice amount: To accept weekly invoices < $5k we need a one-time setup in our billing system; otherwise weekly invoices must meet a $5k floor or else we aggregate into the next month.

Next steps: I’ve looped in Marissa (AM) and Karthik (pricing ops) to confirm discount thresholds and the net45 escalation path. If you’re available, let’s do a 20-min call today at 2:00pm PT to run Procurement through the PO template and confirm the GL mapping.

Best,

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Thanks for the context. Recommended responses / concessions below: 

Discount tiers (aggregate across buckets):
- Tier A: 7% off list if combined committed ARR >= $500k/year (usage + reserved counted together).
- Tier B: 12% off list if combined committed ARR >= $1.2M/year.
- Tier C: 18% off for > $2.5M/year (exec approval).

Net45: We can accept net45 for this account after Finance completes a short underwriting review. We'll need Procurement to sign the updated billing addendum that includes the net45 term and references the PO ID pattern. Request: mark "Net45 request - finance review" in the HubSpot deal so Finance can prioritize.

Invoice cadence / minimums:
- Operationally we can issue weekly consolidated invoices per BU, but we require a minimum invoice amount of $5k. For weekly runs under $5k we either: (a) aggregate into the next billing period or (b) set up a one-time weekly invoice waiver (manual setup + $250 setup fee). Recommend option (a) unless the customer insists on weekly micro-invoices.

PO line detail / ERP mapping:
- Acceptable. We will require a CSV mapping (sample provided during the call) and require the PO to include a "Billing entity" and a single canonical PO ID field that appears on every invoice.

Other recommendations:
- Offer a 60-day pilot credit for the first month for them to validate weekly invoicing flow (helps reduce their risk).
- If they commit to Tier B within 30 days, offer to waive the $250 setup fee and provide a one-time onboarding credit equal to one week's expected invoice (capped at $15k).

I’ll create a HubSpot task and a short addendum template that Priya / Legal can send to Procurement for signature.

-Karthik
Lead, Pricing & Packaging — Redwood Inference

Marcus — quick summary and proposal after internal review: 

1) Invoice cadence: We can support weekly consolidated invoices per BU. By default we require a $5k minimum per weekly invoice; if Greenspire needs invoices under $5k we can enable a weekly micro-invoice workflow with a one-time $250 setup fee. As an alternative we can aggregate weekly charges into monthly invoices if you prefer to avoid the setup.

2) Net terms: Redwood standard is net30. We can accept net45 pending Finance underwriting and signature of a short billing addendum. Please mark Net45 in the PO and provide the PO ID pattern — Finance will then complete the review.

3) PO line detail: We will include SKU-level line items with unit price, quantity, and a field for your GL code. Please share the SKU -> GL mapping CSV (or populate the attached tab in your PO spreadsheet) and a sample of your ERP invoice ingestion file.

4) Discount stacking: We can allow aggregation across usage + Dedicated / Reserved capacity for discount slabs. Proposed thresholds (for discussion): 7% at $500k ARR, 12% at $1.2M ARR; 18% for > $2.5M (requires exec approval). If you can commit to Tier B within 30 days we'll waive the weekly setup fee and provide a one-time onboarding credit (details to be in the addendum).

Next steps:
- Can you confirm whether Procurement is okay with the $5k weekly minimum or wants the micro-invoice setup?
- Please share the SKU->GL mapping CSV and example ERP sample so we can validate invoice ingestion.
- If net45 is required, please indicate that in the PO and we'll route to Finance.

I’m available for a 20-minute call tomorrow at 10:00am PT to walk the PO template with Procurement. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and include a short addendum draft.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.
